'''''Nymphaea'' × ''khurooi''''' is an artificial hybrid of ''[[Nymphaea alba]]'' and ''[[Nymphaea odorata]]'',<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" /> which has been naturalised in India.<ref name = "COL" />

==Description==
===Vegetative characteristics===
''Nymphaea'' × ''khurooi'' is a perennial,<ref name = "Flowers of India">''Nymphaea'' x ''khurooi'' - Meghalaya Red Water Lily. (n.d.). Flowers of India. Retrieved June 14, 2025, from https://www.flowersofindia.net/catalog/slides/Meghalaya%20Red%20Water%20Lily.html</ref> rhizomatous<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /> aquatic<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" /> herb with a horizontal rhizome.<ref name = "Flowers of India" /> The petiolate leaf with an entire margin<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /> and rounded basal lobes<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" /> has impressed veins.<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /> The leaf surface does not have a mottling pattern.<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /> The juvenile leaves display bronze colouration.<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" /> The petiole has four central air canals.<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" />
===Generative characteristics===
The small, red flowers<ref name = "Flowers of India" /> has a peduncle with five central canals.<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /> The flowers have 23–28 petals.<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /><ref name = "Flowers of India" /> The androeceum consists of 75–100 stamens<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /><ref name = "Flowers of India" /> with 20 mm long filaments and yellow-orange anthers.<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" /> The gynoeceum consists of 17–22 carpels.<ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011" /><ref name = "Flowers of India" /> It is sterile.<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" /><ref name = "Flowers of India" /> 

==Taxonomy==
It was described by [[Milind Madhav Sardesai]] and [[Mayur Dhondiram Nandikar]] in 2020.<ref name = "IPNI">''Nymphaea'' × ''khurooi'' Sardesai & Nandikar. (n.d.-b). International Plant Names Index. Retrieved June 13, 2025, from https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77212176-1</ref><ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020">Nandikar, M. D., & Sardesai, M. M. (2020). ===Etymology===
The hybrid name ''khurooi'' refers to Anzar Ahmad Khuroo from the [[University of Kashmir]].<ref name = "IPNI" /><ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" />
===Hybridisation===
It is a hybrid of ''[[Nymphaea alba]]'' and ''[[Nymphaea odorata]]''.<ref name = "IPNI" /><ref name = "POWO" />

==Distribution==
It has been naturalised in India<ref name = "COL" /><ref name = "Dkhar et al., 2011">Dkhar, J., Kumaria, S., & Tandon, P. (2011, January). [https://www.researchgate.net/publication/235218918_Nymphaea_alba_var_rubra_is_a_Hybrid_of_N_alba_and_N_odorata_as_Evidenced_by_Molecular_Analysis ''Nymphaea alba'' var. ''rubra'' is a hybrid of ''N. alba'' and ''N. odorata'' as evidenced by molecular analysis.] In Annales Botanici Fennici (pp. 317-324). Finnish Zoological and Botanical Publishing Board.</ref> (Meghalaya, Jammu & Kashmir), where it occurs in lakes.<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" />

==Habitat==
It occurs in lakes.<ref name = "Nandikar & Sardesai, 2020" />
